member.name: M:Graphs.Coupling.Cauchy.Evaluate(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: J = 1 / (1 + d² / δ²). Heavy-tailed — decays much slower than Gaussian. Retains weak long-range coupling that Gaussian would zero out.

member.name: M:Graphs.Coupling.Gaussian.Evaluate(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: J = exp(-d² / 2δ²). Smooth, differentiable decay. Natural choice for Euclidean-geometry metrics.

member.name: M:Graphs.Coupling.Laplacian.Evaluate(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: J = exp(-d / δ). Decays on distance, not distance². Sharper local contrast than Gaussian — near neighbors are favoured more aggressively.

member.name: M:Graphs.Coupling.Linear.Evaluate(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: J = max(0, 1 - d / δ). Compact support — exactly zero beyond one scale length. Hard locality boundary; no long-range coupling whatsoever.
